cells.tense: The strength you lean on has been tested many times and is still here, and you're with it right now.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Carry the next piece of some stretch that's taking longer than you wanted, on your own. Do your part, report nothing, and ask nobody how you're doing.
cells.core:
Where you stand with people, you feel with them instead of just about them, and you stay. That's the shape your strength takes here — not a push on anyone, just staying while the hard thing keeps being hard. The waiting isn't patience exactly. You keep showing up because you decided to, and the deciding holds. Around you people stop bracing, and they can't say why.

Some stretch of yours is taking longer than you wanted. Carry the next piece of it on your own, without asking anyone how you're doing, and stop there. The load gets lighter, in your own hands, quietly. You'll notice you didn't need an audience for it. Nothing in that asks anyone for a feeling; it just keeps the going going.
cells.sheetLine: You stay with people because you decided to, not because it's easy.
cells.verb: keep going on what you hoped for, after the hoping has gone anyway
cells.place: standing beside someone without having to fix what they feel

cells.tense: You will keep going toward what you hoped for, and you are already rehearsing how long that will take.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Set the one you're straining toward and the plain fact that it isn't here yet side by side on paper, then shut the notebook for a day.
cells.core:
Your staying is real, and lately it's got a hard edge. In the place where you feel alongside people, you've started carrying the next stretch before it arrives, working out how you'll hold when it comes, who'll need what. People can feel the grip in it. You're still beside them, but you've moved ahead of them to the part you'd rather meet first — and what you hope for keeps receding, because you keep standing where it hasn't landed.

Set the two down. Write what you're straining toward, and underneath it the plain fact that it isn't here yet. Shut the notebook and keep it shut for a day — no planning, no telling. Both are true, and you don't have to pick one to stand on. What waits gets a moment of not being pushed, and you get to find out which one you're actually reading from.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing further ahead than the day you're in.

cells.tense: You stood beside people while it mattered, and you're still at a doorway you already walked through.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Pick something you look after that's gone slack — a plant, a room, a standing appointment. Give it ten quiet minutes, neatly, and stop when the ten are up.
cells.core:
There was a stretch when you could feel your way alongside people, kept the hope going, and it held. Lately you've been somewhere else when you're with them. You still sit down at the table, but you answer from a step behind, and it costs more than it should. The strength in you isn't gone. It's been spending itself while nothing it cares about gets fed, and a person can't keep company on what's left after that.

So put something back in. Pick something you look after that's gone slack — a plant, a room, a standing appointment. Tend it for ten quiet minutes, neatly, and stop when the ten are up. You'll be doing it for your own sake, not theirs. Steady hands come back through the thing being cared for, and then you're able to be beside someone again without leaving early.
cells.sheetLine: The strength isn't gone, but what you look after has gone unfed.
cells.verb: keep going on what you hoped for, after the hoping has gone anyway

cells.tense: You are already carrying the pressure for people near you, and you call it just getting through the week.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: When you sit with someone and start taking their side of it onto your shoulders, put it back. Carry what's yours and let theirs stay theirs.
cells.core:
You don't flinch when things get tight, and the people near you have felt the benefit without seeing you do any of it. You've told people it's nothing special, that anyone would do the same, and you mostly believe that. Meanwhile the ones who rely on you have been quietly relying on something rather specific, and you've filed it under the week being hard. It's yours. You'd give credit for it easily to someone else.

Next time you're sitting with someone and their problem is landing on your shoulders, put it back. Carry your own part, and let theirs stay theirs. It might sound strange the first time. The hand you need for your own load is the one you've been lending. You can say no to theirs without moving away from them.
cells.sheetLine: What you call getting through the week is something people lean on.
cells.verb: keep going on what you hoped for, after the hoping has gone anyway
cells.place: standing beside someone without having to fix what they feel
